_meta.note: Agent roster. This is configuration, not demo data: it describes the intended architecture. 'implemented' means a model-backed agent exists and runs; 'stage' says how. model = settled. beta = the model calls run and are still being watched. deterministic = an engine under app/services does the job with no model at all, which is not the same claim and is not made as one. The researcher and the data scientist stay deterministic on purpose: a hypothesis is written from a template rather than by a model reading the data it is about to be tested on, and the statistics are arithmetic. A model in either place would not be a better agent, it would be a worse guarantee.

agents.name: observer
agents.role: Reads an anomaly the detectors already found
agents.question: What does this measurement look like?

agents.name: researcher
agents.role: Turns anomalies plus memory into falsifiable hypotheses
agents.question: What could explain this?

agents.name: data_scientist
agents.role: Builds the dataset and runs the test
agents.question: Does the data support it?

agents.name: critic
agents.role: Attacks the result before anyone believes it
agents.question: Why might this be wrong?
outputs: critic verdict PASS | NEEDS_MORE_DATA | FAIL (stricter only)

agents.name: writer
agents.role: Drafts public messages from real results only
agents.question: Is there something worth communicating?

agents.name: reviewer
agents.role: Final gate before anything becomes public
agents.question: Is every claim in this supported by a stored result?
